generic_name: Insulin Syringe with Needle, Disposable, 0.3 mL
purpose: This is a small, single-use syringe used to inject insulin for people with diabetes. It holds up to 0.3 mL of insulin, which is perfect for smaller doses. It helps you accurately measure and deliver your insulin dose under the skin.
how_it_works: The syringe has a very thin, short needle that goes just under the skin into the fatty tissue. You draw up your prescribed amount of insulin into the barrel, then inject it so your body can absorb it and help control your blood sugar. The 0.3 mL size is designed for doses of 30 units or less.
common_side_effects: You may notice minor pain, redness, or a small bruise at the injection site. Rotating where you inject can help prevent skin bumps or hardening called lipohypertrophy over time.
warnings: Never reuse a disposable syringe — the needle becomes dull and increases your risk of infection and pain. Always dispose of used syringes in a proper sharps container, never in regular trash. Keep syringes away from children. Make sure you are using the correct syringe size that matches your insulin concentration (usually U-100).
typical_dosing: Use one syringe per injection as directed by your doctor. Draw up only the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Inject into the fatty area of your abdomen, thigh, or upper arm, and rotate sites each time.
